videos.title: Yo ya no persigo las noticias: ahora vienen a buscarme
videos.description:
En este vídeo les presento cMRSS, una aplicación accesible que permite reunir en un mismo lugar las fuentes de noticias y contenidos que realmente nos
interesan.
Podemos añadir medios y páginas mediante sus fuentes RSS, organizar lo que seguimos y consultar las novedades sin tener que ir saltando de una web a otra.
Pero hay una función que a mí me ha gustado especialmente: también podemos añadir canales de YouTube y seguir sus nuevas publicaciones desde la propia
aplicación, sin necesidad de entrar continuamente en YouTube para comprobar qué han publicado.
cMRSS no es gratuita, y eso también hay que decirlo. Pero después de usarla y comprobar lo que me ofrece, en mi caso considero que merece la pena la inversión.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona, qué posibilidades ofrece y por qué se ha ganado un sitio entre las aplicaciones que utilizo para mantenerme informado.

videos.title: TifloAcosta ya tiene app: todo cambia a partir de aquí
videos.description:
TIFLOACOSTA APP — ACCESO DIRECTO
Este enlace abre directamente TifloAcosta App. No necesitas descargar ningún archivo ni registrarte para entrar. Desde ahí puedes utilizar la aplicación en el navegador y, si quieres, instalarla en tu dispositivo para tenerla disponible como una app más.
TifloAcosta da hoy uno de los pasos más importantes desde que comenzó este proyecto.
Durante mucho tiempo hemos ido creando vídeos, cursos, guías, documentos, recursos en español y en inglés y una comunidad que sigue creciendo. El problema es que todo ese material estaba repartido entre distintos lugares.
Ha llegado el momento de empezar a reunirlo.
TifloAcosta ya tiene su propia app.
Desde ella puedes buscar recursos por palabras, recorrerlos por categorías, consultar las novedades, guardar tus favoritos y acceder al catálogo completo de vídeos del Canal TifloAcosta.
Además, la aplicación se ha pensado desde el principio teniendo en cuenta la accesibilidad y el uso con lectores de pantalla.
En este vídeo te enseño cómo funciona, qué puedes encontrar dentro y cómo puedes instalarla para tener TifloAcosta mucho más cerca.
La demostración práctica se realiza en iPhone utilizando VoiceOver, y también explico cómo acceder e instalarla desde Android y Windows.
Si quieres entrar directamente mientras ves el vídeo, este es nuevamente el enlace:
La aplicación seguirá creciendo.
Iremos incorporando nuevos recursos, mejorando lo que ya existe y ajustando aquello que la experiencia real de los usuarios nos vaya indicando.
Porque esto no pretende ser simplemente otra página donde acumular enlaces.
La idea es mucho más ambiciosa: crear un lugar estable, accesible y sencillo desde el que entrar a todo lo que TifloAcosta va construyendo.
Hasta ahora, TifloAcosta era principalmente un canal, una comunidad y una colección de contenidos repartidos por distintos espacios.
Desde hoy empieza a tener su propia casa.
Y acabamos de abrir la puerta.

videos.title: Este atajo no pregunta, ve un código y se pone a investigar
videos.description:
Ponle un código delante… y a ver qué pasa
Hoy les traigo uno de esos atajos que empiezas haciendo para resolver una cosa y al final termina haciendo bastante más de lo previsto.
La idea es sencilla: encontrar un código y averiguar qué contiene.
Puede trabajar con códigos que estén en una imagen o una captura guardada en el iPhone, pero también con códigos que tengamos delante y podamos captar con la cámara.
Y no nos quedamos únicamente con los códigos QR.
El atajo también puede reconocer códigos de barras y, cuando encuentra información que merece la pena investigar, utiliza Internet para intentar averiguar qué hay detrás de ese código y ofrecernos información útil.
Por ejemplo, podemos encontrarnos un código de barras en un producto y querer saber qué es, o recibir una imagen que contiene un QR sin tener otro teléfono disponible para escanearlo.
La intención ha sido precisamente esa: tener una herramienta sencilla y accesible que podamos lanzar desde el iPhone y dejar que haga el trabajo.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona y las distintas posibilidades que ofrece.
IMPORTANTE:
Para utilizar este atajo es necesario tener instalada la aplicación gratuita Actions, ya que algunas de las funciones que utiliza el atajo proceden de esta aplicación.
Descargar Actions desde la App Store:
Instalar el atajo:
Una vez instalada Actions, conviene abrirla al menos una vez. Si sus acciones no aparecen posteriormente en la aplicación Atajos, reinicien el iPhone.
Como siempre, este atajo lo comparto para que puedan probarlo, jugar con él y, sobre todo, sacarle partido.
Tony Acosta
Canal TifloAcosta

videos.title: VoiceOver: ¿Esa voz es nueva?
videos.description:
VoiceOver no tiene por qué quedarse únicamente con las voces que trae el iPhone.
En este vídeo pruebo dos formas de ampliar su repertorio: las voces de Visionauta, una aplicación de reconocimiento del entorno que permite incorporarlas al sistema, y Runa TTS, una nueva plataforma que todavía se encuentra en fase beta y no está disponible en la App Store.
Escucharemos cómo suenan y qué posibilidades ofrecen para darle a VoiceOver un registro diferente.

videos.title: Un ciego prevenido vale por dos: alertas sísmicas en el móvil
videos.description:
En este vídeo hablo de algo que ojalá no tengamos que necesitar nunca, pero que conviene conocer: cómo puede ayudarnos el móvil a recibir avisos relacionados con terremotos.
Primero explico qué opciones existen en Android y en iPhone para recibir alertas en tiempo real cuando hay un terremoto cerca, siempre dependiendo del país, la cobertura y los sistemas oficiales disponibles.
Después presento una aplicación llamada Earthquake, disponible para iPhone y Android, que permite hacer seguimiento de movimientos sísmicos, consultar información sobre terremotos, avisos de tsunami y otros datos útiles. La app se puede usar con VoiceOver y puede resultar interesante para quienes quieran estar informados desde el móvil de forma accesible.
No se trata de vivir con miedo, sino de saber qué herramientas tenemos a mano cuando la tierra decide moverse sin pedir permiso.

videos.title: Actualizaciones invisibles en iPhone: qué son y por qué importan

Estas actualizaciones no requieren descargar una versión completa del sistema ni reiniciar el dispositivo. Se aplican de forma automática y están diseñadas para corregir fallos de seguridad urgentes, actualizar bases de datos internas o mejorar el funcionamiento de servicios clave.
Se encuentran dentro de Ajustes, General, Actualización de software, y dependen de una opción llamada “Respuestas de seguridad y archivos del sistema”. Si está activada, el iPhone puede recibir mejoras sin que el usuario tenga que hacer nada.
En este vídeo se explica qué son exactamente estas actualizaciones, qué cambian en el dispositivo, por qué Apple las utiliza cada vez más y qué ventajas tienen frente a las actualizaciones tradicionales de iOS.

news.title: WeWalk Smart Cane 2: la nueva generación del bastón inteligente ya está a la venta
news.summary: La tecnología aplicada a la movilidad de las personas ciegas y con baja visión continúa avanzando. Una de las novedades que ha llegado es el WeWalk Smart Cane 2, la nueva generación del bastón inteligente desarrollado por WeWalk, que incorpora mejoras en detección de obstáculos, navegación, controles físicos y asistencia mediante inteligencia artificial. El nuevo […] La entrada WeWalk Smart Cane 2: la nueva generación del bastón inteligente ya está a la venta se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
La tecnología aplicada a la movilidad de las personas ciegas y con baja visión continúa avanzando. Una de las novedades que ha llegado es el WeWalk Smart Cane 2 , la nueva generación del bastón inteligente desarrollado por WeWalk, que incorpora mejoras en detección de obstáculos, navegación, controles físicos y asistencia mediante inteligencia artificial.

El nuevo dispositivo ya está en el mercado y ya está siendo presentado en diferentes eventos europeos de tecnología asistiva. En octubre podrá probarse, por ejemplo, en eventos especializados celebrados en Dublín y Londres.

El WeWalk Smart Cane 2 mantiene la utilización del bastón blanco como herramienta principal de movilidad, pero añade sensores y funciones digitales para proporcionar información adicional al usuario.

Una de sus funciones principales es la detección de obstáculos situados por encima del nivel del suelo , como ramas, señales u otros elementos que podrían encontrarse a la altura del pecho o de la cabeza.

La compañía afirma que el nuevo modelo mejora un 30 % la precisión y el enfoque de la detección de obstáculos respecto a la generación anterior.

Es importante señalar que esta función no sustituye las técnicas tradicionales de utilización del bastón. El propio fabricante indica que el sensor no está diseñado para detectar desniveles, escalones, bordillos o agujeros en el suelo, por lo que continúa siendo necesario utilizar correctamente el bastón blanco para detectar este tipo de elementos.

Una de las modificaciones más visibles está en el propio diseño del dispositivo.

El Smart Cane 2 es aproximadamente un 25 % más ligero y un 40 % más delgado que su predecesor. Además, incorpora resistencia frente a las condiciones meteorológicas y una nueva disposición de los controles.

Mientras que el primer WeWalk utilizaba una superficie táctil, el nuevo modelo apuesta por botones físicos , algo que puede facilitar la interacción y hacer que determinadas funciones sean más fáciles de localizar mediante el tacto.

El fabricante también ha incorporado un altavoz tres veces más potente que el del modelo anterior y una linterna integrada.

Las alertas pueden recibirse mediante sonido y vibración , con diferentes posibilidades de personalización.

Una de las funciones más interesantes del ecosistema WeWalk es la navegación mediante voz.

Cuando el bastón está conectado al teléfono móvil y a la aplicación WeWalk, el usuario puede recibir indicaciones paso a paso para desplazarse hasta diferentes destinos.

El sistema también proporciona información relacionada con el transporte público. Entre otras posibilidades, puede informar sobre rutas y ayudar a seguir un trayecto en transporte público, incluyendo avisos relacionados con el momento en el que hay que bajarse.

Esta función puede resultar especialmente interesante en desplazamientos por entornos desconocidos, ya que permite recibir las indicaciones directamente desde el bastón sin tener que sostener el teléfono.

El modelo básico tiene un precio de 699 € e incluye las principales funciones inteligentes del bastón, como la detección de obstáculos elevados, la conectividad con el teléfono móvil y las funciones de navegación.

También existe la posibilidad de añadir una suscripción anual de 129 € que incorpora las funciones de inteligencia artificial y sus correspondientes mejoras.

Además, WeWALK ofrece la posibilidad de reservar una clase online de formación para aprender a utilizar el dispositivo , con un precio de 129 €.

En cuanto a la adaptación física, el bastón puede personalizarse según la altura de la persona usuaria, con medidas disponibles desde 119 hasta 150 centímetros , para conseguir un ajuste más adecuado a cada usuario.

Otra de las grandes novedades del Smart Cane 2 es la incorporación de un asistente de inteligencia artificial basado en Gemini .

La interacción se realiza mediante voz y permite formular preguntas relacionadas con el entorno o solicitar información.

Según WeWalk, el asistente puede utilizarse, por ejemplo, para:

De esta manera, el bastón incorpora una capa adicional de asistencia basada en inteligencia artificial, que se suma a las funciones de movilidad y navegación.

El nuevo dispositivo se comercializa en dos configuraciones.

Por un lado está el WeWalk Smart Cane 2 , que incorpora las funciones principales de detección de obstáculos, navegación, información sobre transporte público, lugares cercanos, iluminación y conectividad con el teléfono.

Por otro lado, el WeWalk Smart Cane 2 AI añade acceso ilimitado al asistente de inteligencia artificial integrado.

También es posible adquirir el modelo estándar y añadir posteriormente el acceso al asistente mediante una suscripción.

Aunque el Smart Cane 2 incorpora sensores y funciones avanzadas, WeWalk insiste en que debe utilizarse manteniendo las técnicas habituales de movilidad con bastón.

El sistema de detección de obstáculos está pensado para proporcionar información adicional, pero no puede detectar todos los peligros presentes en el entorno. Por ejemplo, la propia documentación del dispositivo advierte de que el sensor no detecta desniveles del terreno como escaleras, bordillos o agujeros.

Por este motivo, el Smart Cane 2 debe entenderse como una herramienta complementaria al bastón blanco tradicional , no como un dispositivo que sustituya la formación en orientación y movilidad.

El WeWalk Smart Cane 2 refleja una tendencia cada vez más presente en la tiflotecnología: la incorporación de sensores, navegación, conectividad móvil e inteligencia artificial en dispositivos que las personas ciegas ya utilizan habitualmente.

Su llegada prevista para noviembre permitirá comprobar cómo responden las personas usuarias a esta combinación de movilidad tradicional, detección de obstáculos, navegación mediante voz e inteligencia artificial .

El nuevo modelo ya está siendo mostrado en eventos especializados de tecnología asistiva y se espera su lanzamiento comercial a principios de noviembre de 2026.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

news.title: How to help stop spam calls on iPhone and Android
news.summary: Spam calls don't have to grab your attention and waste your time. Use these built-in options to silence and block them without having to pay.
news.body:
Spam calls are apparently here to stay, but you have ways to fight back.

Spam calls should be a bygone concern, but unfortunately they're still a plague many of us deal with. Services like Truecaller have helped with caller identification and spam filtering for years. But since Android and iOS have gotten great at handling spam calls on their own, you don't need to rely on a third-party app — much less pay a subscription — to avoid unwanted callers.

In addition to functions on your phone, your carrier may offer its own spam protection features. Depending on the company, these might be enabled by default. If not, check your online account or the carrier's app for a spam protection toggle.

If you have an iPhone, navigate to Settings > Apps > Phone . The most important option is under the Call Filtering section; enable Spam and calls that your carrier identifies as junk won't ring. They'll be automatically sent to voicemail, and in the Phone app's Calls tab, they appear under the Spam section (accessible under the top-right button).

To further keep your call logs tidy, enable the Unknown Callers option in the same Settings box. With this, recent calls from non-contacts appear under the Unknown Callers section (available via the mentioned top-right button in the Phone app). Use Mark as Known to remove a given number from this section if needed.

Back on the Settings page, review the Screen Unknown Callers section, where you have three options. Never is the default, where every incoming call rings normally. The most aggressive approach is Silence , which mutes all incoming calls from numbers not saved in your contacts and sends them to voicemail. You can view these silenced calls on the same Calls tab of the Phone app.

Ask Reason for Calling is a good middle ground; with this, your iPhone will screen unknown callers and ask them why they're calling. You're able to view a live transcript of the caller's response on your screen and decide whether the call is worth answering. Call Screening is only available in select countries on iPhones running iOS 26 or newer.

While you presumably have friends and family saved in your contacts already, make sure to save any other numbers that contact you regularly, like doctors' offices or work clients. These options are great for shutting up spammers, but you'll need to be a little more vigilant to avoid missing legitimate calls from unsaved numbers.

Most Android phones offer spam detection for calls, although availability and capabilities vary depending on your phone's model, its Android version and the dialer app you use. The official Phone app by Google is what most Android manufacturers ship with their devices, and it comes with caller ID and spam detection built-in. If your phone uses a different dialer, poke through its settings to look for a similar solution, or download Google's Phone app and set it as the default dialer.

Launch the Phone app, tap the hamburger menu (three horizontal lines) at the top-left and choose Settings . Under the Call Assist section, tap Caller ID and spam . Here, enable See caller and spam ID to have the app warn you of an incoming potential spam call before you answer it. To go further, enable Filter spam calls to automatically silence suspected junk calls.

You can still view missed calls and voicemails from unknown callers in the Phone app. For both of these features to work, you'll need a phone running Android 6.0 or newer, with the latest version of the Phone app by Google installed and set as the default.

Some Android phones, including ones from Samsung and Google, feature enhanced call screening options akin to the Ask Reason for Calling feature on iPhone. If you own a Pixel 6 or newer, launch the Phone app and navigate to Settings > Spam and Call Screen > Call Screen to set up this feature. On supported Samsung phones, open the Phone app, tap the three-dot icon in the top-right corner and navigate to Settings > Call screening .

news.title: Apple reportedly worked with LG on gadgets for its upcoming smart home push
news.summary: The doorbell, security cameras, thermostats and more could be announced next week.
news.body:
The doorbell, security cameras, thermostats and more could be announced next week.

We've been hearing a lot about Apple's renewed smart home endeavors from Mark Gurman at Bloomberg over the past few months, and he's back today with a report that the company co-developed several new gadgets in partnership with LG Electronics. Based on recent regulatory filings by LG, Bloomberg reports that the results of this collaboration are expected to include a smart doorbell, a smart thermostat, a smart deadbolt lock, indoor and outdoor security cameras, and a floodlight camera. Rather than Apple's iconic fruit symbol, the hardware will reportedly be sold under LG's banner, with the South Korean business responsible for the devices' manufacturing and product support.

This smart home slate is expected to be unveiled next week , and the LG product lineup is likely to center around a new hub device from Apple that has been in development for several years . A revamped HomePod Mini and TV set-top box may also be coming as part of Apple's move toward offering a bigger system of connected home tech. While the Apple-branded devices are expected to be available soon, Bloomberg says the LG accessories won't hit the market for "at least a few more months."

This co-development effort also marks a shift for LG. The brand has long been known for appliances and large electronics rather than smart home products. LG has been a partner for Apple in other verticals in the past, such offering Apple software via its smart TVs and serving as a third-party monitor option for the MacBook ecosystem. It also produces the panels for Apple's current lineup of Mac monitors, the Studio Display and Studio Display XDR .

news.title: iFixit tears down Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, finds mixed repairability results
news.summary: Concluding iFixit’s teardown sequence for Apple’s September launches, iFixit today published the teardown of the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Here’s what they found. more…
news.body:
Concluding iFixit’s teardown sequence for Apple’s September launches, iFixit today published the teardown of the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 . Here’s what they found.

After applying heat to the new Apple Watch Ultra 4 ’s screen, iFixit’s Shahram Mokhtari uses the company’s new metal pick to pry the screen open, exposing the battery and the Taptic Engine.

He notes that replacing the 2.444 Wh battery (versus 2.313 Wh in the Ultra 3) still requires removing the screen, which remains a significant repairability drawback. The four screws on the bottom of the case provide access only to the sensor assembly on the underside of the back cover and the S11 chip on the case itself.

Once the screen is unglued, though, removing the battery and disconnecting the display’s press connector seems straightforward enough, provided that the initial step was done carefully enough to avoid slicing through any of the flex cables underneath.

That said, with no significant improvements in repairability, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 scored 4/10 on iFixit’s repairability scale, the same as its predecessor.

iFixit’s teardown of the new Apple Watch Series 12 revealed a slight repairability improvement, with Apple adding stretch-release adhesive and a pull tab that make the 1.461 Wh battery (versus 1.403 Wh in the 46mm Series 11) easier to remove.

Still, as with the Apple Watch Ultra 4, the Series 12 also requires prying off the glued display to get inside, which remains the biggest obstacle to repairs. Mokhtari noted that the tolerances around the Series 12 ’s display are even tighter than on the Ultra 4, requiring enough force to make him concerned about potentially damaging the screen.

Mokhtari also noted that Apple replaced the ZIF connector and tape used for the display on previous models with a simpler press connector.

The tradeoff is that replacing the screen now also requires removing and replacing the battery, “which, if you’ve come this far, why wouldn’t you?” he adds.

All in all, the modest repairability improvements were enough for iFixit to give the Series 12 a 4/10 repairability score, a 1-point bump from the last base-model Apple Watch it scored.

For comparison, iFixit gave Google’s Pixel Watch 5 a 9/10 repairability score, noting that its display can be removed with just two Torx screws and a gasket, while its battery can also be removed without dealing with adhesive.

news.title: Remember MapQuest? You can now use it with Android Auto
news.summary: If you use Android Auto, you can try out the beta mapping service today.
news.body:
If you use Android Auto, you can try out the beta mapping service today.

Launched in 1996, MapQuest, the world's oldest commercially available web mapping service, recently introduced Android Auto support, making it an alternative to Google and Apple Maps with the added distinction of calling a certain body of water in North America Lake Ontario, despite pressure from President Donald Trump.

The decision to retain the lake's 380-year-old name drew a lot of attention. While both Apple and Google bowed to that pressure and changed how the name appears to map users in the US, MapQuest did not. This refusal prompted a huge spike in interest in its service, the company said. Usage grew to 50 times its normal rate, and the apps it offers generated over 1.5 million downloads. MapQuest quickly became the No. 1 mapping app on Apple's App Store. "Hundreds of thousands of people signaled to us this weekend that we got it right, by downloading our app," said Doug Berger, general manager of MapQuest in a statement.

The company is feeding this interest with the introduction of beta support for Android Auto on Google Play.

Once these steps are complete — including joining the beta program — you should find MapQuest available to you in your vehicle.

Initial user feedback on MapQuest's Android Auto beta suggests the application remains a little rough around the edges in comparison to Google or Apple Maps. Various reports claim there have been complaints of app crashes, delayed response times and voice navigation prompts that cut off in the middle of sentences. Interface quirks have been identified, and there may be some frustration that some real-time features are limited to North America (US and Canada).

To be fair, this is beta software; flaws and foibles are to be expected, and the company's social media feeds suggest its developers are actively working to improve the app, including regular software patches.

news.title: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT outputs by default—but only in the EU
news.summary: Like other solutions, it is not especially reliable, and it's easy to circumvent.
news.body:
OpenAI will begin automatically watermarking text generated with ChatGPT in the European Union, the company has announced. It will also offer the watermarking feature in other regions, but it will be off by default outside of the EU.

The move in Europe is driven by a need to comply with the EU AI Act, which took effect in August. It requires marking content produced by AI models in a way that another tool can detect. Unfortunately, there is still no completely effective and reliable way to do that. A few standards already exist, like SynthID and the C2PA project, but they are relatively easy to circumvent for anyone with basic know-how.

The same is likely true for OpenAI's watermark. Its method is proprietary; the company calls it textGrain, and has published a technical paper explaining how it works. But in general, it works like other LLM watermarking tools we've seen in the past: It puts patterns in the word choices that are not clear to a human reader, and that don't meaningfully change the general quality of the output, but that someone with a key can use a specialized detector to find. OpenAI says it will be giving access to the detector to a limited number of researchers and organizations, and providing a request-for-approval process for others to be added over time.

news.title: Silicon Valley’s AI wunderkind launches Underdog, the most private Instinct/Muse competitor yet
news.summary: Sigil Wen, backed by a Silicon Valley who's who, has built an on-device AI assistant that promises to be free, fully private, and capable for everyday tasks.
news.body:
When self-taught coder Sigil Wen was 17, he moved to Silicon Valley and lived in an AI hacker house with famed AI researcher Andrej Karpathy.

While there, he hacked and coded alongside other people who would become the biggest names in AI, like Perplexity founder Aravind Srinivas and OpenAI researcher Noam Brown. He tested early versions of AI tools that would later become well known, including a chatbot shared by Anthropic co-founder Ben Mann that would become Claude, an image generator from David Holz that would become Midjourney, and what would become OpenAI’s GPT-3 and the image generator Stable Diffusion. Prominent investor and entrepreneur Naval Ravikant hired him for Airchat, Ravikant’s now-defunct rival to the Clubhouse social network.

For fun, he figured out how to get GPT-2 running on his Apple Watch. “It was a magical time,” Wen told TechCrunch.

Now a Thiel Fellow — the program from investor Peter Thiel that invites young founders to pursue projects instead of college — Wen on Monday launched an invite-only beta of Underdog, one of the most private AI assistants Silicon Valley has yet to offer. The model runs wholly on-device, meaning the user’s data remains on devices they already own, currently Macs and Windows PCs, with Linux, iPhone, and Android versions coming soon.

Wen built Husky, an inference engine, or software that runs AI models, and Husky is designed to run fast. Unlike other on-device engines, Wen says, it moves less data between the computer’s main chip and its graphics chip.

Underdog has other security features baked in, too, like encrypting the keys to the email and other accounts that users authorize Underdog to access.

Underdog is, however, using much smaller models than today’s state-of-the-art ones hosted in data centers. It currently uses a 27-billion parameter reasoning model fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B.

Wen argues that this model compares favorably with Claude Opus 4.6 in some benchmarks , or what was considered top performance six months ago. He says that means it can handle the everyday tasks that people want an AI assistant to do, like shopping research or answering math homework questions.

“You don’t need to sacrifice your privacy for the capability because they’re just as capable,” Wen says. He adds that small on-device models will continue to grow more capable over time.

Perhaps the most interesting thing about Underdog is its early business model. The app will be free at first and never ad-supported. Since the AI runs on users’ machines, Underdog doesn’t have the giant overhead of paying a provider for inference. “I don’t have to charge you a subscription to run this because my costs are so super low,” he said.

Instead, with Stripe co-founder Patrick Collison as one of his angel investors, he’s borrowing a play from the fintech era. Underdog will take a tiny percentage of payment transactions that the AI assistant makes using Stripe’s secure payment rails, something like an interchange fee. In this way, the AI assistant never has to mine your data. It is as aligned with you as your bank or credit card providers.

This runs contrary to the business motivations of many of the other players in AI assistants, whose privacy policies allow them to collect data on users that they may sell to advertisers or other third parties, or use to train other models.

That kind of data collection could be a particularly treacherous trade-off for users of an AI assistant, which may need access to the most intimate details about you in order to be useful, from medical conditions to financial data to data on your kids.

As Wen wrote in what he calls his AI manifesto , “Why should using AI require surrendering your private information?”

He tells TechCrunch: “I honestly want to build Underdog for myself. I’m building a product that I would be proud for my future children to use.”

The startup behind Underdog is named Conway Research, and Collison isn’t its only big-name investor. Conway is backed by Andreessen Horowitz via partner Chris Dixon, as well as Khosla Ventures, Hummingbird, SV Angel, the Anthology Fund (the partnership fund between Menlo Ventures and Anthropic), and a prominent list of angel investors that includes Vercel founder Guillermo Rauch, Noam Brown, and Deedy Das, among others.

news.title: How AI decision models could change content moderation
news.summary: On Tuesday, Musubi announced a lightweight decision model made for real-time moderation called PolicyLM-1.7B, released with open weights.
news.body:
As decision models spread across the industry, a company called Musubi has a new idea for how to put them to work: moderating content. On Tuesday, Musubi announced a lightweight decision model made for real-time moderation called PolicyLM-1.7B , released with open weights.

The idea is to take a content policy written in plain English and apply it to messages in under 50 milliseconds. Musubi’s model is designed to be similar in cost and speed to the AI classifier systems that power moderation on most social platforms — but because it has the flexibility of a modern LLM, it can apply complex policies without special training. Even more important, the model won’t need new training when the policy changes, allowing for human policy-setters to iterate as much as they need.

As Musubi co-founder and chief AI officer Filip Jankovic sees it, it gives platform managers a way to label content proactively.

“Product teams just want a better understanding of what’s happening on their platform, especially as the amount of content is exponentially increasing,” Jankovic says. “Being able to label all of that in a very scalable, customizable way is extremely useful.”

Decision models have become a hot topic in the AI world since the release of TypeSafe AI’s Jev in September , which was shortly followed by competing decision models from OpenAI and Amazon . Instead of outputting text, a decision model outputs outcome probabilities, though in this case the model outputs a binary judgement: Either the content is in the category or it isn’t. By limiting the model’s output to a set of predetermined choices, decision models are able to run faster and cheaper than large language models, while still maintaining the flexibility of the transformer architecture.

One early use case is reining in misbehavior by AI agents — so it’s only natural to apply the same technology to human misbehavior.

Notably, Jankovic says his interest in decision models predates Jev, tracing it back to a 2024 project called GLiNER (Generalist Model for Named Entity Recognition) that deployed many of the same techniques.

Still, Musubi isn’t wary of the comparison. If anything, the company is eager to use the new interest in decision models to shine a light on content moderation. “If Jev caught your eye, PolicyLM-1.7B is the same kind of model, trained specifically for content moderation, that you can run yourself,” the product announcement reads.

news.title: The next hurdle for AI agents: getting websites to let them in
news.summary: Personal AI agents promise to shop, book flights, and make reservations for you. But deliberate blocks and anti-bot defenses are getting in the way, leaving consumers caught in the middle. A new standard aims to help.
news.body:
Personal AI agents, like Meta’s Muse, Instinct, ChatGPT’s Dots, and others, are kicking off a new wave of consumer AI that involves more than just responding to queries. These AI agents can actually get things done on users’ behalf, like booking flights, making dinner reservations, ordering groceries, and more, all without having to be technical enough to set up OpenClaw or some other agent on your own computer.

But consumers adopting these agents are often running into issues when the website on the other end of their request blocks the AI from completing the job.

Most recently, Amazon began blocking Meta’s Muse AI agent from its retail site, meaning that the agent could no longer browse or make purchases from its product catalog.

However, the problem is not limited to Amazon or Muse. User complaints across social media indicate their agents are often running into similar blocks. Some of these are intentional, like Amazon’s, while others are the result of websites’ traditional anti-bot measures designed to protect against spam and malicious activity.

What’s not clear to the end user is whether or not the block is accidental on the website owner’s part, which leaves them frustrated with both the service provider or retailer and the agent trying to facilitate the transaction.

For instance, TechCrunch has seen a han d ful of complaints on social media claiming that Muse couldn’t complete a purchase on Walmart’s retail website. ( NBC also reported that this was a problem Walmart had faced in its tests of the AI agent.)

But a spokesperson for Walmart told us these weren’t intentional. In fact, Walmart is partnered with Muse, as was announced at Meta’s Connect developer conference in September. The company said it wants to be where its customers are, and that now includes being available through AI agent experiences.

The issue that Walmart customers often appear to be running into (see below) is that the website presents a button that has to be clicked to verify the visitor is human. If that experience is interrupted, the check could fail, and the agent gets booted out.

It’s an indication that the current technology we use to verify humans and keep websites safe from spam and bots may not be the best fit for the agent-first era of the web we’re now moving into.

To address this problem, industry partners including Meta, Walmart, Stripe, Sierra, Genesys, Rocket, NiCE, and Decagon have begun working on an open standard that would dictate how AI agents can communicate with businesses, helping to separate the good bots acting on behalf of the user and the bad. This protocol will be specifically focused on agent-to-agent communication for the purposes of online commerce, Meta said in a blog post.

In the meantime, consumer confusion abounds.

Although Walmart is at least trying to be accessible via AI agents, other companies aren’t so keen on the idea or haven’t fully embraced the technology.

For example, flight booking is currently one of the main use cases being positioned for agents, but many people have reported issues with airlines rejecting their agents’ requests.

Delta, for instance, told us that the company is taking steps to protect customers from unauthorized automated activity, and that if it were to open up to AI agents, it would have to be done with “security and the customer experience in mind.”

“While Delta does not currently have a partnership or integration that enables a third-party AI agent to shop for or book Delta flights on a customer’s behalf on our digital platforms, we’re continuing to evaluate how new technology, including external AI agents, could enhance the way customers engage with Delta,” said Delta’s general manager of Global Communications, Heena Chavda, in response to our questions about whether or not it was blocking agents, as some users complained.

United was not quite as direct as Delta, but a spokesperson pointed us to the part of its Terms of Use policy, which says that the user agrees “not to use any robot, spider, other automatic device, or manual process to monitor or copy this website or the content contained therein or for any other unauthorized purpose without United’s prior written permission.” (United didn’t respond to a follow-up question about whether it was blocking specific personal AI agents, like Muse.)

Early adopters’ complaints across social media have referenced a number of brands that are reportedly blocking AI agents, including Yelp , eBay , Zillow , Pizza Hut , Adidas , and various airlines . Some believe that the blocking activity seems to have recently increased .

A couple of people even said eBay suspended their accounts because of their use of agentic AI. Another complained that Google kicked out Instinct while it was cleaning up their Gmail inbox for them.

Despite the push to have agents book tables at restaurants and other tedious tasks, Yelp told us that it doesn’t permit non-human traffic on its platform unless the agent has paid to access Yelp’s content and data through its data licensing program . That means agents trying to use its site to get a quote, add a user to a waitlist, or book them a table will likely fail if they don’t have a formal partnership with Yelp.

eBay told TechCrunch that its approach is not to prohibit all third-party shopping agents from completing purchases. Instead, its policies restrict unauthorized agents and actions, like automated scraping and model training.

Adidas, Zillow, and Pizza Hut either didn’t respond or declined to provide a comment by the time of publication.

One major company involved in this space is Cloudflare, which offers sites protection from AI agents that could be training on its data and managing other automated activity. Some suspect that Cloudflare and other content delivery networks (CDNs) like it are currently disrupting Muse traffic. This is attributed to a change to crawler defaults on September 15, which allows site owners to block AI training while allowing other types of bots. Existing sites that were previously set to block AI bots for security reasons were then shifted to block AI agents on any pages that had ads.

However, when we asked if Cloudflare had any insight into what was happening with the blocking of these personal AI agents, like Muse and others, the company said it didn’t have any specific data to share at this time. It pointed us instead to its free public data hub, Cloudflare Radar . The site shows the increase in bot activity (which Cloudflare has also commented on previously), but it doesn’t help differentiate between the good bots and the bad ones.

Cloudflare also has a vested interest in mitigating AI traffic to websites, as it now runs a marketplace where AI bots have to pay for the data they access. It recently began testing a new web browser built specifically for AI agents.

Given the rapidly evolving space, Meta’s decision to form specific brand partnerships for Muse access seems to be the right way to go, as is its decision to focus on new standards. In doing so, it assures its customers that its agent, at least, is welcome at these partners’ sites — so any issues with access would be reportable bugs.

Meta also maintains a list of “connectors” (a.k.a. partners) inside the Muse app, which continues to grow. Many of Meta’s newly announced partners haven’t yet shown up in this list. But given Muse’s rapid expansion , which now includes partnered tools for small businesses , a bigger reorganization of Muse’s connector list is likely soon to be underway.

“Turning away a personal agent means turning away the customer behind it. We’d rather work with businesses to address the underlying concerns than see them lose that customer,” Meta said in its announcement about the newly announced plans to develop a standard. “There is a path that is good for users and good for businesses. It starts with clear norms, gives businesses more predictable control, and evolves toward a more efficient way for agents to work together.”

news.title: Googlebook "Better Together" phone features don't work with Samsung at launch
news.summary: Googlebooks require Android 17, but Samsung's Android 17 phones won't work yet.
news.body:
Googlebooks are Google's latest attempt to carve out a piece of the premium laptop market, and tight integration with Android phones is a key part of that effort. Now that Googlebooks are available, we're learning of some frustrating limitations of that plan. For now, Googlebooks will only play nicely with your phone if you have a Pixel.

When Google announced the launch window for Googlebooks, it said the laptops were "engineered to work with your Android phone right out of the box." But as with many things Google, the truth is more convoluted. We have since learned that you need Android 17 for any of the nifty integrations to work. With a compatible Android 17 phone, you can seamlessly stream apps to your laptop, access files on your phone, mirror notifications, and continue where you left off in certain apps when switching from phone to laptop.

You might think that the latest Samsung phones, which shipped with Android 17, would be ready for this experience. You'd be wrong, though. Some early Googlebook adopters have complained that phones like the Z Fold 8 won't work with the laptops. While the devices appear to see each other, the phone doesn't stay connected. Google representatives have since confirmed that these "Better Together" features are not currently supported on even the latest Samsung phones. An update that brings support to Samsung phones will roll out in "the coming weeks."

news.title: All-electric camping gets a solar upgrade: The 2027 Pebble Flow
news.summary: The Pebble Flow has a 45 kWh LFP battery and can even charge an EV.
news.body:
There is, I think, a pent-up demand for bringing electrification to camping. Anyone who’s had their sleep disturbed by the sound of someone else’s generator running at night would probably agree.

Certainly, any time we cover an electric van , comments are filled with people wondering if and when a camper conversion might appear. Kia showed off such a concept a couple of years ago , as did Winnebago , and Volkswagen is adding a camper trim to its electric ID. Buzz. And then there’s the world of trailers. Colorado Teardrop sadly didn’t make it, and some other electrified trailers remain in development. But for a couple of years, you’ve been able to buy the Pebble Flow . And for 2027, it’s getting an update.

Introduced in 2025, the streamlined Flow is built atop a 45 kWh LFP battery pack that, for 2027, can be recharged by up to 4 kW of solar panels, which Flow says should be sufficient to generate more electricity than you’ll use in an average day of camping. Earlier Flows could be specced with an optional 1.1 kWh panel on the roof; the new kit adds another 2 kWh via four portable panels.

news.title: Ya disponible la cuarta beta de NVDA 2026.3
news.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la beta 4 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la cuarta beta de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la cuarta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
news.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 4 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 4 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 8be91476179710c4abffe5094459df9be1696d92e5d6cd0ace47d52321bb87ab. ¡Feliz martes!

La entrada Ya disponible la cuarta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

news.title: Monarch 2.0 lleva la IA al braille y los gráficos táctiles
news.summary: HumanWare ha lanzado Monarch 2.0, una importante actualización de su dispositivo de braille multilineal y gráficos táctiles, con nuevas funciones de inteligencia artificial y mejoras para explorar matemáticas, gráficos y contenidos digitales. El Monarch combina 10 líneas de braille con gráficos táctiles dinámicos en una misma superficie, permitiendo acceder mediante el tacto a información que […] La entrada Monarch 2.0 lleva la IA al braille y los gráficos táctiles se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
HumanWare ha lanzado Monarch 2.0, una importante actualización de su dispositivo de braille multilineal y gráficos táctiles, con nuevas funciones de inteligencia artificial y mejoras para explorar matemáticas, gráficos y contenidos digitales.

El Monarch combina 10 líneas de braille con gráficos táctiles dinámicos en una misma superficie , permitiendo acceder mediante el tacto a información que tradicionalmente se presenta de forma visual. La actualización 2.0 fue anunciada por HumanWare el 14 de septiembre de 2026.

Monarch es un dispositivo de tecnología de apoyo desarrollado por HumanWare en colaboración con la American Printing House for the Blind (APH) y la National Federation of the Blind (NFB) .

Su característica principal es combinar braille multilineal y gráficos táctiles en una única pantalla dinámica. El dispositivo cuenta con 10 líneas de 32 celdas de braille , además de una superficie formada por miles de puntos que permite representar información gráfica mediante el tacto.

De esta forma, una persona puede explorar mediante el tacto textos, diagramas, mapas, gráficos y contenidos matemáticos , sin depender exclusivamente de materiales impresos o gráficos táctiles estáticos.

Una de las novedades de Monarch 2.0 es Describe with AI , una función capaz de generar una descripción verbal de una imagen .

Esta herramienta se incorpora al visor de gráficos táctiles y permite obtener información mediante una descripción generada por inteligencia artificial.

La función puede resultar especialmente interesante cuando se trabaja con contenidos que contienen información visual y puede complementar la exploración táctil.

No obstante, HumanWare no presenta Describe with AI como un sustituto de la representación táctil . Se trata de una función de descripción de imágenes integrada en el dispositivo.

Monarch 2.0 también incorpora mejoras destinadas a facilitar el acceso a información matemática y gráfica.

El visor de gráficos KeyMath ha sido rediseñado para ofrecer más detalle y simplificar la exploración de gráficos. Además, la integración de MathCAT mejora la conversión de contenidos matemáticos entre la representación impresa y el braille.

Por otro lado, Tactile Viewer incorpora nuevos niveles de zoom para determinados gráficos, incluidos los archivos SVG .

Esto permite ampliar las posibilidades de exploración de diagramas y otros contenidos gráficos mediante el tacto.

Las nuevas funciones pueden tener especial interés en el ámbito educativo.

El Monarch está diseñado para que estudiantes ciegos y con baja visión puedan acceder a contenidos que tradicionalmente presentan importantes barreras de accesibilidad, como gráficos, mapas, diagramas, ecuaciones o libros de texto digitales .

La actualización también incorpora un modo examen , que permite al personal educativo seleccionar qué aplicaciones y herramientas puede utilizar el estudiante durante una evaluación.

De esta manera, el alumno puede seguir utilizando las capacidades de braille y gráficos táctiles del Monarch mientras se restringe el acceso a determinadas herramientas durante una prueba.

Monarch 2.0 introduce mejoras en el intercambio y la colaboración mediante KeyDrive y añade estilos integrados para archivos eBraille en VictorReader.

Estas mejoras buscan facilitar el acceso a documentos digitales y ampliar las posibilidades de trabajo con contenidos en braille electrónico.

La evolución del Monarch muestra cómo diferentes tecnologías de apoyo pueden combinarse en un mismo dispositivo.

Hasta ahora, acceder a determinados contenidos visuales podía requerir disponer de un gráfico táctil específicamente preparado. Con Monarch, los usuarios pueden explorar gráficos dinámicos y braille en una misma superficie, mientras que Describe with AI añade una vía adicional para obtener información verbal sobre imágenes .

Para ámbitos como la educación, las matemáticas, la lectura de gráficos o el acceso a información visual, esta combinación puede abrir nuevas posibilidades de interacción con contenidos digitales.

La actualización Monarch 2.0 ya ha sido anunciada por HumanWare y amplía las funciones del dispositivo con herramientas centradas en braille, gráficos táctiles, matemáticas e inteligencia artificial.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

news.title: Shortcut Menu
news.summary: Shortcut Menu lets the Android accessibility shortcut, such as holding both volume keys, turn your choice of screen reader or other accessibility service on or…
news.body:
Published 3 October 2026 by Kareen Kiwan

Shortcut Menu lets the Android accessibility shortcut, such as holding both volume keys, turn your choice of screen reader or other accessibility service on or off. It works like the accessibility shortcut menu on iPhone:

Turning a screen reader on turns any other screen reader off, so two never talk at once. Services with the same name, such as Google’s and Samsung’s TalkBack, are told apart by their maker, such as “TalkBack (Samsung)”. Pressing the shortcut again while the menu is open closes it.

Without Shortcut Menu, a shortcut with more than one feature on it asks which one to use, and that question is not spoken when no screen reader is on.

With Shizuku, run the same command without adb shell. In Settings, Accessibility, open Shortcut Menu and turn on its shortcut, such as the volume keys. Make Shortcut Menu the only feature on that shortcut. Open the Shortcut Menu app and choose which services the menu offers. Until you choose, it offers your screen readers. The app also shows whether the permission is granted and what each shortcut is assigned to, and has a button to try the menu. How it works The shortcut turns Shortcut Menu’s accessibility service on, and the service opens the menu. When the menu closes, the service turns itself off, so the next press turns it on again. A press while the menu is open turns the service off, which closes the menu.

Choosing a service changes Android’s list of enabled accessibility services directly, so Android does not ask “Allow full control?” each time. The menu speaks with the phone’s text-to-speech engine, at the accessibility volume.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Samsung UI is the only Android UI that offers 3 accessibility shortcuts: pressing and holding the volume keys, short pressing the power and volume up keys, and the accessibility onscreen button or gesture, based on the navigation mode being used. Other OEMs offer only the first and third shortcuts. Honor even excludes the accessibility button and gesture, leaving the user with only 1 shortcut, and that shortcut can only be assigned to 1 accessibility service. On UIs that allow more than 1 accessibility service to be assigned to the shortcut, Android asks the user to choose which one to activate every time the shortcut is used. However, this dialog is not accessible if no screen reader is running.

Shortcut Menu aims to address these shortcomings by allowing the user to choose the accessibility services they want to launch from the shortcut. The user can then launch any of the selected services in an accessible way. When no screen reader is active, the service speaks the items as the user moves their finger over them, and lifting the finger activates the selected service. If a screen reader is already active, the service makes sure to turn it off before launching another screen reader to avoid potential conflicts.

Setting up the app requires an ADB command, which can be run either using ADB on a computer or directly on the phone through an ADB app that uses wireless debugging. Working with ADB is not covered here, but I personally used the ADB AppControl mobile app to enter the command that grants the app the required permission.

The app's UI is straightforward. It shows whether the permission has been granted and which shortcut is assigned to the service. It also includes a menu where you can turn services on or off without using the shortcut. The user can select which services should be included, although screen readers are checked by default. For me, Jieshuo Main, Jieshuo Helper Service, TalkBack, and AI Subtitles were all included.

When using the shortcut, the app currently speaks through Google TTS. When a screen reader is active, it behaves like a regular screen that the screen reader can interact with.

For Samsung users who keep both Samsung TalkBack and Google's TalkBack on their devices and wish to switch between them, both can be added to the services list. I haven't tested this on a Samsung device to see if there are any issues. Anyway, starting with One UI 9, Samsung TalkBack is replaced with Google TalkBack, so there are no longer two TalkBack versions.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

App version: 0.2, Android 16

No accessibility ratings yet. Be the first to rate this app.

Please use this rating only for accessibility. For feedback about the app’s features, price, overall quality, or your general experience, use the comments section below.

Please log in to rate this app’s accessibility.

news.title: DelveKin: Dungeon Defense
news.summary: The heroes are coming. Build a dungeon worthy of stopping them! DelveKin is a charming dungeon defense strategy game where you take the role of the Dungeon Master. Design your defenses, place traps, command monsters, and battle invading heroes across handcrafted encounters and replay-able dungeon challenges. BUILD YOUR DUNGEON - Choose rooms with different layouts and tactical advantages, then fill them with monsters and traps. Every placement matters as heroes advance deeper into your dungeon. COMMAND YOUR MONSTERS - Take direct control during turn-based battles. Move across the battlefield, launch basic attacks, unleash special abilities, and combine your monsters' strengths to overcome each group of heroes. SET CLEVER TRAPS - Slow heroes with snares, strike from the walls with arrow slits, or punish careless movement with hidden hazards. Traps can shape the battlefield and create opportunities for your monsters. GROW YOUR ARSENAL - Unlock new monsters, traps, rooms, and powerful bosses as you progress. Earn experience, level up your defenses, and build stronger dungeon teams for the challenges ahead. FACE NEW HEROES - Each stage introduces different hero combinations, abilities, and tactical threats. Adapt your dungeon to withstand knights, mages, rogues, clerics, and other determined adventurers. VENTURE INTO DEEP DELVE - Put your dungeon building skills to the ultimate test in Deep Delve, a replay-able 20-depth challenge where every run is different. Build a run specific roster, recruit and replace monsters and traps, choose powerful upgrades, evolve your boss, and see how deep your dungeon can survive. CONTINUE INTO DUNGEON RAIDS - Complete the main campaign and enter Dungeon Raids, where increasingly dangerous hero parties push your defenses even further. CHARMING ART STYLE - DelveKin features expressive characters, lively battle animations, and a playful fantasy world. Play the opening chapters for free. A single Premium unlock opens the full campaign, additional progression, Dungeon Raids, and Deep Delve. Build carefully. Fight cleverly. Protect your dungeon.

news.title: LUCID: inteligencia artificial para aprender Braille
news.summary: La inteligencia artificial también está abriendo nuevas posibilidades en el aprendizaje del Braille. Un ejemplo es LUCID, un sistema de aprendizaje diseñado por el Product Experience Design Lab (PXD Lab) de la Universidad de Houston, en Estados Unidos. La propuesta combina interacción táctil, una pantalla Braille y orientación mediante audio asistida por inteligencia artificial. Su […] La entrada LUCID: inteligencia artificial para aprender Braille se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
La inteligencia artificial también está abriendo nuevas posibilidades en el aprendizaje del Braille. Un ejemplo es LUCID , un sistema de aprendizaje diseñado por el Product Experience Design Lab (PXD Lab) de la Universidad de Houston , en Estados Unidos.

La propuesta combina interacción táctil, una pantalla Braille y orientación mediante audio asistida por inteligencia artificial . Su objetivo es acompañar a las personas ciegas y con baja visión desde el aprendizaje de las primeras letras hasta la práctica de la lectura.

El proyecto ha recibido además un Red Dot Award en la categoría de Inclusive Design , un reconocimiento internacional relacionado con el diseño de soluciones innovadoras.

LUCID es un concepto de tecnología asistiva para el aprendizaje del Braille desarrollado por el equipo del PXD Lab de la Universidad de Houston.

El sistema está formado por dos dispositivos complementarios: LUCID-ALT y LUCID-ARC . Cada uno está pensado para una etapa diferente del aprendizaje.

La idea es que la persona pueda avanzar progresivamente, comenzando por el reconocimiento de los caracteres Braille y pasando después a ejercicios de lectura con una pantalla Braille de tamaño real.

La primera parte del sistema es LUCID-ALT .

Se trata de un dispositivo con un teclado ampliado de seis puntos , basado en la estructura de la celda Braille. El usuario puede explorar mediante el tacto las diferentes combinaciones de puntos y familiarizarse con la formación de las letras.

Este planteamiento pone el tacto en el centro del aprendizaje , en lugar de sustituir la experiencia Braille por una interacción exclusivamente sonora.

A medida que la persona progresa, el sistema plantea una transición hacia una experiencia de lectura más cercana a la que encontrará posteriormente en una pantalla Braille convencional.

La segunda parte es LUCID-ARC , que incorpora una pantalla Braille de tamaño real .

Su función es permitir que el aprendizaje avance desde el reconocimiento de letras hacia la práctica de la lectura. De esta manera, el usuario no se queda únicamente en ejercicios básicos con los seis puntos, sino que puede familiarizarse progresivamente con una experiencia de lectura más próxima a la de otros dispositivos Braille.

Según la Universidad de Houston, esta transición pretende preparar al estudiante para las herramientas que utilizará fuera del proceso de aprendizaje.

Uno de los elementos más llamativos de LUCID es la incorporación de inteligencia artificial como apoyo durante el aprendizaje .

El sistema utiliza orientaciones y comentarios de audio en tiempo real para acompañar al usuario mientras realiza los ejercicios. La intención es ofrecer indicaciones durante la práctica y reducir la necesidad de contar continuamente con un instructor al lado.

De esta forma, LUCID combina dos vías de interacción:

La Universidad de Houston explica que esta combinación busca favorecer una práctica más autónoma y permitir que cada estudiante avance a su propio ritmo.

Uno de los aspectos más interesantes de LUCID es que no plantea la inteligencia artificial como sustituta del Braille.

Al contrario, el sistema mantiene la experiencia táctil como elemento fundamental y utiliza la IA como apoyo durante el proceso de aprendizaje.

Esto resulta especialmente relevante en un contexto en el que cada vez existen más herramientas tecnológicas basadas en voz. Para las personas ciegas y con baja visión, la tecnología puede facilitar el acceso a la información, pero el Braille continúa siendo una herramienta fundamental para la alfabetización, la lectura y la escritura.

La propuesta de LUCID busca precisamente combinar ambos mundos: la información sonora que puede proporcionar la inteligencia artificial y la información táctil que proporciona el Braille .

El proyecto ha sido reconocido con un Red Dot Award en la categoría de Inclusive Design .

El reconocimiento corresponde al trabajo de la diseñadora Varshini Chouthri y del profesor Min Kang , director del Product Experience Design Lab de la Universidad de Houston.

Para el PXD Lab, este reconocimiento se suma a otros proyectos relacionados con el diseño centrado en las personas y la tecnología.

Es importante hacer una aclaración.

LUCID no debe confundirse con un producto comercial que ya pueda adquirirse. La información publicada por la Universidad de Houston presenta el proyecto como un sistema diseñado por su laboratorio y muestra representaciones del dispositivo. No hemos encontrado información oficial que indique que esté actualmente disponible para su compra o implantado de forma generalizada en centros educativos.

Por tanto, hablamos de una propuesta de diseño y tecnología asistiva , no de un producto que actualmente podamos recomendar para aprender Braille.

LUCID forma parte de una tendencia más amplia: el desarrollo de herramientas de inteligencia artificial que pueden utilizarse como apoyo para las personas ciegas y con baja visión.

La American Foundation for the Blind (AFB) ha analizado durante 2026 el uso de inteligencia artificial por parte de personas con discapacidad. Sus investigaciones muestran que la IA ya se utiliza para tareas como leer textos, describir imágenes y facilitar el acceso a información, aunque también advierten de problemas relacionados con la accesibilidad, la precisión y la necesidad de supervisión humana.

En este contexto, propuestas como LUCID muestran otra posibilidad: utilizar la IA no solamente para describir el mundo visual , sino también para acompañar procesos de aprendizaje relacionados con la tecnología asistiva .

La evolución de la tiflotecnología no consiste únicamente en desarrollar gafas inteligentes, aplicaciones de navegación o herramientas capaces de reconocer imágenes.

También implica buscar nuevas formas de aprender, leer y escribir de manera accesible .

LUCID plantea precisamente esta combinación entre Braille, tecnología háptica, audio e inteligencia artificial . Aunque todavía no se trata de una solución comercial disponible para el público, su diseño muestra una posible dirección para las futuras herramientas de aprendizaje accesible.

La tecnología puede cambiar la forma en la que utilizamos el Braille, pero propuestas como LUCID ponen el foco en algo fundamental: la tecnología debe servir para facilitar el acceso al aprendizaje sin dejar de lado la experiencia táctil que hace posible la lectura y escritura Braille.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

news.title: AppleVis Unlimited: What's New and Noteworthy for September 2026

This newsletter features a curated selection of community-submitted content, including new app entries, updates, news, podcast episodes, and popular discussions. We hope that you find this publication to be both helpful and informative. If you have any questions or feedback about this newsletter, please feel free to reach out using our Contact Form . AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month: Restaurant Rush: Cook & Serve Restaurant Rush is a simulation game that puts you in charge of your very own restaurant: preparing orders, serving customers (before they lose patience), earning coins, upgrading your kitchen, and building your way to different restaurants. With a 100-day campaign, Endless mode, more than 50 recipes, kitchen upgrades, and waitstaff to hire (and more), there is plenty here to keep you busy. And all of it comes from a developer who is passionate about accessibility and engagement with our community. Read more about Restaurant Rush here. Brainclash is a quiz game with a different rhythm: a refined battle of minds you take on in your own time, with no pressure. Challenge a friend to a match, let the game pair you with a random opponent, or train first against the computer. Play unfolds turn by turn: you answer, then your opponent answers, and the most accurate one wins. There's no tense timer forcing you both online at the same moment — take your turn whenever you like, and return for the next one anytime. Play cards onto a 5×5 board, build poker hands (pairs, straights, flushes, full houses, and the rare royal flush) and turn every hand into damage. Fully playable with VoiceOver, every tile and every move is spoken. No ads, no lives, no timer. Nothing you buy helps you play. Final Fortress is a match-3 puzzle. A working console in the dark, the hum of the systems, static like rain. A watch takes fifteen or twenty minutes: do the day's tasks, read what came in, hand over. Welcome to the September 2026 edition of AppleVis Unlimited, your monthly digest of the latest and most notable content on the AppleVis website. This newsletter features a curated selection of community-submitted content, including new app entries, updates, news, podcast episodes, and popular discussions. We hope that you find this publication to be both helpful and informative. If you have any questions or feedback about this newsletter, please feel free to reach out using our Contact Form .

Restaurant Rush is a simulation game that puts you in charge of your very own restaurant: preparing orders, serving customers (before they lose patience), earning coins, upgrading your kitchen, and building your way to different restaurants. With a 100-day campaign, Endless mode, more than 50 recipes, kitchen upgrades, and waitstaff to hire (and more), there is plenty here to keep you busy. And all of it comes from a developer who is passionate about accessibility and engagement with our community.

Read more about Restaurant Rush here.

From the App Store:

New here? Challenge a friend, answer whenever you wish, and let the sharpest mind win. Multiple categories, and a daily reward waiting for you.

Brainclash is a quiz game with a different rhythm: a refined battle of minds you take on in your own time, with no pressure. Challenge a friend to a match, let the game pair you with a random opponent, or train first against the computer. Play unfolds turn by turn: you answer, then your opponent answers, and the most accurate one wins. There's no tense timer forcing you both online at the same moment — take your turn whenever you like, and return for the next one anytime.

Additional Details:

Additional Details:

Chess you already know. An army you have to raise.

Chess Meets Necromancy is a turn-based roguelike played on a real chessboard with real chess movement. Your hero is one piece. Everything you capture is a corpse you can raise.

Additional Details:

Keep useful text, links, formatting and images close at hand, with accessible local history and optional encrypted synchronization through your own Clipman Server.

Clipman is an accessible clipboard manager for iPhone and iPad. It keeps useful text, links, formatting and images close at hand without turning clipboard history into a complicated, mouse-first workflow.

Use Clipman locally without creating an account, or connect to an optional self-hosted Clipman Server to share encrypted clipboard history between your iPhone and iPad.

Additional Details:

Featured in Apple's "New Games We Love". Now with the Daily Three: the same three fights for everyone, one attempt a day. Offline, ad-free, one purchase.

The city runs on cards. Time to make your name.

Cyphr City is a cyberpunk card RPG where poker is combat and the whole city is up for grabs. Play cards onto a 5×5 board, build poker hands (pairs, straights, flushes, full houses, and the rare royal flush) and turn every hand into damage. Both hands are face-up, so every card is a chess move: read the board, block their line, and drop the 5th card to steal a hand right out from under them.

Additional Details:

Connect dots. Outthink the bot. Challenge a friend. Try Magic bonuses, race the clock in Rush, or sharpen your tactics in Practice.

Every move changes the match. Connect dots, outthink the bot, or challenge a friend in tactical soccer.

Move the ball between adjacent dots and plan around routes that have already been used. Reach one of your opponent's three goal dots to score. Put the ball in your own goal and the other side gets the goal.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Match-3 on the screen of an old terminal. Fully playable with VoiceOver, every tile and every move is spoken. No ads, no lives, no timer. Nothing you buy helps you play.

Final Fortress is a match-3 puzzle. The whole game is the screen of an old terminal: green text, one cursor, and you, the commandant of the last fortress.

It is a quiet game. A working console in the dark, the hum of the systems, static like rain. A watch takes fifteen or twenty minutes: do the day's tasks, read what came in, hand over. Nothing hurries you, and nothing happens while you are away. Come back after a week and the fortress is exactly as you left it.

GameBoard is a premier, audio-first multiplayer gaming platform designed to bring players together through classic card and board games. Crafted with universal accessibility in mind, GameBoard is 100% compatible with native mobile screen readers like VoiceOver, while offering a visually stunning, responsive interface for all players. Play Ludo, Mile by Mile, Farkle, Citadels, and more with friends or competitors worldwide. Whether you play by sight, sound, or touch, GameBoard provides an equal, inclusive, and exciting competitive environment.

Bring your manuscript to life. Organize chapters, track your writing, and compile Markdown files into books, documents, presentations, and braille.

ghostWriter Markdown is an accessibility-first, plain-text writing app for notes, articles, documentation, and full manuscripts. Write individual documents, organize chapters, and compile your work into a finished export.

VoiceOver was at the center of the design from the first line of code. Created by a blind developer, ghostWriter gives screen reader users and anyone who loves plain text a clean, native place to write.

What happens when you take classic Hangman and turn up the pressure? You get Hangman Blitz, the classic word-guessing game, reimagined. Classic Hangman The game you know and love. Guess the hidden word one letter at a time, but choose carefully, you don't want to complete the figure. Timed Hangman Think you've mastered Classic? Unlock Timed Hangman and try it with a two-minute clock counting down. Guess the word before the figure is completed, or before the clock hits zero. Blitz Mode Now go all-out. The hangman figure is gone, the clock is ticking, and your goal is simple: guess as many words as you can before time runs out. Correct letters add precious seconds; mistakes take them away. Work your way through Starter, Rapid, and Extreme Blitz, where the clock gets shorter and the penalties get tougher.
